beats: Cast rule (episodes/e01-moe/FACTS.md: an expert is not a topic specialist; never label one by subject): the receptionist plus eight doctors told apart only by face and hair, no specialty props; the film numbers the doors in code (#0-#255), never names a department.

Hook (0-5 s): Qwen3-235B has 3.4x the parameters of Llama 3 70B, yet uses 22B per token, under a third of 70B: a small clinic with a doctor busy in every window next to a tower 3.4x bigger where only a few windows are at work (line_moe_two_buildings).
Cover / title "A huge model that only wakes a few": the receptionist rings the bell in the on-call room and only two of the sleeping doctors get up (line_moe_oncall_bunks).

What MoE is, in Zhongkai's own picture: a hospital. You do not see every doctor; a receptionist (the router) sends you to a few of the doctors (the lecture's word is "specialist"; the drawings never show a specialty) (line_moe_triage_desk). The dense way: every doctor on every patient (line_moe_everyone_consults).

Three milestones: 1991 (Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan & Hinton), 2017 (Google brings MoE into deep networks), 2024 (DeepSeek's fine-grained experts, 256 per layer) (reuse line_grow). Per layer, not per model: every floor has its own receptionist and its own pair of open doors, and one always-open room every patient passes through (the shared expert) (line_moe_floor_triage).

Why the FFN: it holds most of the weights (79.8% of Llama 3 70B, 96.4% of Qwen3-235B): one generalist bent under a mountain of books (line_moe_generalist_books) becomes eight doctors with a small stack each (line_moe_books_split, which is also the cast line-up); line_balance for attention vs FFN.
The trend since 2025: more experts, more sparsity: DeepSeek-V3 opens 8 of 256 doors per layer plus one shared expert (37B per token), Kimi K2 8 of 384 (line_moe_door_wall).

The math in three moves: the router scores every expert (blank cards on every door, the film writes the scores: line_moe_door_score_cards), keeps the top k, and blends their answers by score (line_moe_three_notes, or reuse line_paint_pour for the weighted mix).
Pitfall / cliffhanger: top-k is the one jump in an otherwise smooth network; how do you train a receptionist who only ever picks? (tease L14-02 on line_moe_door_score_cards).
Takeaway: capacity scales, the cost per token barely moves (back to line_moe_oncall_bunks).
Cover (line_cover_l14_01; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the receptionist rings the bell in the on-call room and only two of the sleeping doctors get up.
